classification.difficultyReason: Express the shaded segment as sector minus triangle and combine the two symbolic area formulas by factoring. Earlier supplied practice already establishes this decomposition, so the proof requires routine generalisation.

content.prompt:
The shaded region is called a segment. Prove that its area is given by the formula
$$A=\frac12r^2(\theta-\sin\theta),$$
where $\theta$ is measured in radians.

spec.description: Sector with centre O at the left, equal radii OA and OB bearing matching single ticks and labels r, central angle theta, and vertical chord AB. Light blue shading replaces source grey and identifies only the segment between chord AB and the minor arc.
spec.mathematics: OA=OB=r. The minor segment is the sector AOB with triangle AOB removed. Coordinates determine a schematic figure and introduce no numerical angle given.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied labels, equal-radius marks, central-angle cue and the requested shaded region are visible.

answer.worked:
Area of triangle:
$$A_{\triangle OAB}=\frac12r^2\sin\theta.$$
Area of sector:
$$A_{\text{sector}}=\frac12r^2\theta.$$
The segment is the sector with the triangle removed.
$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{segment}}&=A_{\text{sector}}-A_{\triangle OAB}\\A_{\text{segment}}&=\frac12r^2\theta-\frac12r^2(\sin\theta)\\A_{\text{segment}}&=\frac12r^2(\theta-\sin\theta).\end{align*}$$
